read.call: Modest upside bias: the 10-year is easing from 5.14% toward 5.10%, the chip bounce has follow-through in US futures, and the first big industrial print of the day beat, but Brent near $110 and a 5% ten-year cap any rally.

drivers: Treasury 10-year at about 5.10% this morning after 5.14% Monday, with Fed funds futures at 82% hold and 18% hike for October 28; rates, not data, set the equity tone this week.
Semiconductors ended an eight-session losing streak Monday with the Philadelphia index up 1.6% and the Nasdaq up 1.1%; futures point to modest tech gains.

Europe is the soft spot: ZEW missed, the Stoxx 600 fell 0.8% Monday and the France-Germany spread is 148 bp; Asia was lower overnight with Hong Kong closed.

what_mattered.headline: Chip stocks snapped the longest losing streak since 2008
what_mattered.fact: Philadelphia Semiconductor Index +1.6% Monday after eight straight down sessions that erased about $2.3 trillion of value; Nasdaq +1.11% to 26,431, S&P 500 +0.41% to 7,691, Dow -0.07%.
what_mattered.implication: The AI-capex selloff paused rather than reversed; Netflix tonight and Tesla and Meta later this week decide whether it becomes a trend.

what_mattered.headline: Ten-year Treasury closed at 5.14% and is easing overnight
what_mattered.fact: 10-year yield 5.139% Monday, up about 5 bp; 2-year 4.77%, up 6 bp; both lower early Tuesday with the 10-year near 5.10%.
what_mattered.implication: A 5% ten-year is the valuation ceiling on equities; a 20-year auction tomorrow (prior 5.42%) is the next supply test.

what_mattered.headline: Builder sentiment fell to a 14-year low
what_mattered.fact: NAHB housing market index 29 for October versus 31 expected and 32 prior, the lowest since June 2012; 43% of builders are cutting prices by an average 6%.
what_mattered.implication: Sets a low bar for today's starts and permits; mortgage rates at 7.5% are now hitting supply, which is disinflationary for shelter later but a growth drag now.

what_mattered.headline: China Q3 GDP beat and the PBOC held
what_mattered.fact: GDP +4.5% y/y versus 4.4% expected (Q2 4.3%); September industrial production +5.5% vs 5.4%; retail sales +1.1% vs 0.5%; loan prime rates held at 3.0% and 3.5% for a 17th month.
what_mattered.implication: Beijing gets to keep stimulus on hold, which removes a hoped-for tailwind for commodities and China-exposed industrials.

what_mattered.headline: Europe: ZEW missed and French spreads are at crisis-era wides
what_mattered.fact: German ZEW expectations 28.1 vs 32.0 expected; euro-area 18.5 vs 24.2; France-Germany 10-year spread closed at 148 bp, the widest since the sovereign debt crisis; Stoxx 600 -0.8%, DAX -1.2% Monday.
what_mattered.implication: European risk appetite is deteriorating independently of the US; the ECB's France dilemma is becoming a euro volatility story.

what_mattered.headline: UK jobs data beat
what_mattered.fact: Unemployment 4.7% in June to August versus 4.9% expected; regular pay +3.7%; vacancies -21k on the quarter to 691k; sterling about +0.4% near 1.335.
what_mattered.implication: Reduces the odds of a fast Bank of England easing path and gave the dollar a softer open.

what_mattered.headline: Oil held near a five-month high on Gulf escalation
what_mattered.fact: Brent near $110 with diesel near $200 a barrel; Persian Gulf oil flows at about 80% of pre-war levels per the US Energy Secretary; an LNG tanker was fired on near Yemen and Iran is tightening control of the Strait of Hormuz.
what_mattered.implication: Energy was over half of September's 0.6% CPI jump; oil at these levels keeps the December hike debate alive regardless of today's data.

what_mattered.headline: GM beat and raised the floor of its guidance
what_mattered.fact: Q3 revenue $50.0B versus about $48.8B expected; adjusted EPS $3.70 vs $3.69; EBIT-adjusted guidance narrowed to $14.5-15.5B; adjusted auto free cash flow guidance raised to $11.5-12.5B; new $20B buyback.
what_mattered.implication: The US consumer is still buying trucks at 7.5% financing; a supportive read for industrials and auto lenders into Ally and Capital One.

look_at: Housing starts and permits at 07:30 CT against 1.30M and 1.39M: anything under about 1.25M on starts with permits still falling confirms the NAHB signal and is the day's rates catalyst.
The 10-year around 5.10%: a break back above Monday's 5.14% close into tomorrow's 20-year auction is the one thing that reverses the tech bounce.
Brent near $110 and the 15:30 CT API crude number after last week's 11.1M barrel draw; energy is the swing factor for the November CPI path and the December hike pricing.

GE Aerospace, RTX and Northrop before the open after GM's beat, then Netflix, Capital One and Intuitive Surgical after the close; Capital One's charge-offs are the cleanest consumer-credit read this week.
Pending home sales and the GDPNow update at 09:00 and 10:00 CT: GDPNow at 3.6% versus a housing sector that is contracting is the gap the October 29 GDP print will have to reconcile.

fed.market_pricing: CME fed funds futures on October 20: 82% hold, 18% 25 bp hike, 0% cut for October 28; target range 3.75-4.00% after the September hike; Kalshi and Polymarket show 83-87% hold. Further out, the market prices roughly three 25 bp hikes by July 2027 (Saxo).

themes: Housing recession versus 3.6% GDP: with the NAHB index at 29 (lowest since June 2012) and mortgage rates at 7.5%, today's starts print tests whether residential construction is now subtracting from growth while GDPNow still says 3.6%.
The Fed hike debate moved from October to December: futures price only an 18% chance next week but about three hikes by July 2027 with headline CPI at 3.7% and Brent near $110.
Europe is diverging: euro-area ZEW 18.5 versus 24.2 expected and the France-Germany spread at 148 bp put the ECB's France problem back in front of the euro.
